computational_rule.force: requires explicit RPM, rotor geometry, and rotor mass; no density or mass is inferred
computational_rule.acceleration: requires explicit RPM, rotor geometry, a declared field-response lock, and either total inertial mass or an explicit standalone-rotor condition; mass cancels only when active rotating mass equals total inertial mass
computational_rule.drop_displacement: requires admissible assembly acceleration and an explicit measured fall time or monitored fall distance
computational_rule.realized_vector: requires epoch, lab location, spin-axis attitude, spin sign, and observer velocity state
computational_rule.missing_data: reported as not computable; no substitute values are guessed

papers.citation: J. Luo, Y. X. Nie, Y. Z. Zhang, and Z. B. Zhou, Phys. Rev. D 65, 042005 (2002).
papers.configuration: Double free-fall interferometer; rotating steel gyro versus nonrotating mass; nominal vertical rotor axis.
papers.data: Rotating steel rotor mass 420.0 +/- 2.5 g; CCR mass 76.4 +/- 0.4 g; aluminum frame mass 159.4 +/- 0.9 g; total falling test-mass assembly 655.8 g nominal; rotor diameter about 55 mm; height about 32 mm; 17000 +/- 200 rpm; two 12 m tubes; approximately 10 m monitored path; 20-50 mPa.
papers.reported: No apparent differential acceleration at relative level 2e-6. Horizontal velocity difference estimated below 4.3 mm/s; approximately 6 mm lateral deviation over 10 m used as an upper estimate.
papers.k_status: Source-lock maximum rotor force and complete falling-assembly acceleration/displacement envelopes computed. Exact drop epoch and realized K-Field angle were not reported.
missing_inputs_for_realized_vector: realized spin-axis attitude relative to field response

papers.citation: A. L. Dmitriev, E. M. Nikushchenko, and S. A. Bulgakova, arXiv:0907.2790 (2009).
papers.configuration: Closed falling container with internal horizontal-axis rotor system; speed up to 20000 rpm.
papers.data: Paper states maximum RPM and approximately 14-15 min rotation time; rotor mass, dimensions, exact drop path, exact epoch, and full axis attitude are not supplied in the paper.
papers.reported: Reported average increase Delta g = 10 +/- 2 cm/s^2; stated that geographic north-south versus west-east orientation did not influence results and daily dependence was not observed.
papers.k_status: No K-Field force, acceleration, or displacement computed: rotor geometry/mass and drop trajectory are incomplete.

papers.configuration: Vacuum aviation rotor in isolated container; horizontal-axis measurements over 20-400 Hz; 30 mm fall path.
papers.data: Maximum 400 Hz (24000 rpm); runout 22 min; fall path 30 mm; 40 ms readout; 0.5-1 min sample interval; container 82 x 82 x 66 mm. Rotor mass and rotor geometry are absent.
papers.reported: Reported stochastic frequency dependence, narrow extrema near 320 and 360 Hz, and predominantly negative changes of measured fall acceleration. The paper recommended high-time-resolution ballistic gravimetry using rotating or oscillating test bodies, but reported rotor data rather than a controlled oscillating-mass trajectory experiment.
papers.k_status: No K-Field force, acceleration, or displacement computed: rotor geometry and mass are unavailable.

papers.citation: F. T. Han, T. Y. Liu, X. X. He, and Q. P. Wu, Chin. Phys. Lett. 34, 100701 (2017).
papers.configuration: Proposed concentric hollow aluminum rotating masses in a 3.5 s double-capsule drop.
papers.data: Inner: 27.1 g, radii 15.0/17.5 mm, length 39.92 mm, 2000 rpm. Outer: 69.7 g, radii 25.0/27.5 mm, length 64.37 mm, 20 rpm; speeds may be exchanged.
papers.reported: Conceptual design and uncertainty budget; no completed anomalous drop result. Sensitive x-axis is vertical during drop.
papers.k_status: Source-lock force and individual-test-mass free-response acceleration envelopes computed from explicit mass, geometry, and RPM. No ballistic displacement is computed because the design keeps each mass electrostatically servo-controlled relative to the instrument frame. The K-Field force for a vertical spin axis is horizontal, so the proposed primary vertical channel is geometrically mismatched to that transverse force.
missing_inputs_for_realized_vector: realized spin-axis attitude relative to field response
papers.drop_displacement_computation: not performed because the test masses remain servo-controlled during the proposed drop

papers.citation: T. Liu, Q. Wu, B. Sun, and F. Han, Sci. Rep. 6, 31632 (2016).
papers.configuration: Beijing drop-tower residual-acceleration characterization with single and double capsules.
papers.data: Nearly 3.5 s free fall; double-capsule residual better than 2e-4 g; instrument accuracy better than 4e-5 g.
papers.reported: Ordinary residuals associated with air drag, capsule rotation, accelerometer recovery, and tower airflow structure.
papers.k_status: No K-Field computation: no rotating test mass, RPM, or rotor geometry.

papers.citation: J. Min et al., npj Microgravity 7, 25 (2021).
papers.configuration: Twenty three-axis drop-tower tests of a substitute inertial sensor.
papers.data: Approximately 3.5 s fall; measured approximately 58 micro-g along fall direction and 13 micro-g horizontally in the most stable interval.
papers.reported: 87 micro-g gain-switch transient, approximately 35 nm displacement vibration, approximately 26.56 Hz capsule resonance, and release disturbance.
papers.k_status: No K-Field computation: no rotating test mass, RPM, or rotor geometry.

papers.citation: T. J. Quinn and A. Picard, Nature 343, 732-735 (1990).
papers.configuration: Precision weighing of a freely spinning-down rotor.
papers.data: 330 g rotor, diameter 4.0 cm in Luo compilation, initial speed 8000 rpm.
papers.reported: Apparent mass changes were reduced by more than an order of magnitude and became insignificant after friction-couple and temperature corrections.
papers.k_status: No K-Field computation under the strict rule: the accessible source compilation gives mass, diameter, and RPM but not the complete rotor geometry.
missing_inputs_for_computation: free-fall path or duration for displacement

papers.citation: I. Lorincz and M. Tajmar, Measurement 73, 453-461 (2015).
papers.configuration: High-precision weight measurements with vertical and horizontal rotor orientations.
papers.data: Brass rotor mass 112 g; speed above 25000 rpm in short runs and approximately 19000 rpm in long runs. Complete rotor dimensions are not supplied in the accessible paper text used here.
papers.reported: Precession and vibration artifacts identified; no anomaly within Delta m/m < 2.6e-6.
papers.k_status: No K-Field computation under the strict rule: complete rotor geometry is unavailable.
